title: Majority Frequency Characters
summary: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters, determine the frequency group that contains the maximum number of distinct characters.
statement: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters, determine the frequency group that contains the maximum number of distinct characters. If there are multiple frequency groups with the same maximum number of distinct characters, select the group with the highest frequency count. Return a string containing all characters from the chosen frequency group, in any order.
constraints: s contains one to 100 lowercase English letters.
Group distinct letters by their occurrence count.
Choose the largest group, breaking ties toward the higher occurrence count; return its letters alphabetically.
hints: Count each character first, then invert that mapping into frequency groups.
Compare groups by the pair (number of distinct letters, frequency).
A maximum pair implements both the main rule and the required tie-break; sorting only normalizes the returned order.
Every letter belongs to exactly one frequency group, so comparing those group keys examines every valid answer.
editorial: Every letter belongs to exactly one frequency group, so comparing those group keys examines every valid answer.

tests.explanation: Frequency three contains a and b, more letters than any other group, so return ab.
Frequencies one and two each contain two letters; frequency two wins the tie, so return fp.
